Yalda Night

A Night of Light: Celebrating Yalda at Home

Prepare for the longest night of the year with warmth, delicious Persian flavors, and the timeless tradition of Yalda, celebrating the triumph of light over darkness. This agenda guides you through a cozy evening of feasting, poetry, and togetherness.

  1. Late Afternoon

    Setting the Yalda Sofreh

    Begin preparing your home for the evening by setting a festive sofreh (spread) with pomegranates, watermelons, and candles. This creates a beautiful backdrop for the night's celebrations.

  2. Early Evening (6:00 PM)

    Welcoming Drinks and Appetizers

    As guests arrive or your family gathers, serve the refreshing pomegranate and rosewater cordial, accompanied by a vibrant spread of fresh herbs, feta, walnuts, beet yogurt, and marinated olives.

    Recipes: Pomegranate and Rosewater Cordial · Fresh Herb Platter with Feta and Walnuts · Marinated Olives with Pomegranate and Walnuts · Beet Yogurt Dip with Pistachio

  3. Dinner Time (8:00 PM)

    The Grand Yalda Feast

    Gather around the table for the main course, featuring rich fesenjān, savory tahchin, and a hearty okra stew, complemented by fresh Shirazi salad and warm barbari bread.

    Recipes: Fesenjan (Persian Walnut and Pomegranate Stew) · Saffron Rice Cake with Barberries and Chicken (Tahchin) · Okra Stew (Khoresht-e Bamieh) · Shirazi Salad · Barbari Bread

  4. Late Evening (10:00 PM)

    Storytelling and Sweet Delights

    After dinner, settle in for storytelling and reading Hafez poetry. Enjoy the traditional Yalda fruits and a special mix of nuts and dried fruits for good fortune.

    Recipes: Pomegranate and Watermelon Platter for Yalda Night · Yalda Night Ajeel (Mixed Nuts and Dried Fruits)

  5. Deep Night (Midnight)

    Continued Vigil with Warm Treats

    As the night deepens, keep the vigil going with warm saffron rice pudding, a comforting and aromatic dessert perfect for staying awake and enjoying quiet conversation.

    Recipes: Saffron Rice Pudding (Sholeh Zard)

  6. Pre-Dawn

    Hafez Divination and Reflection

    As the longest night draws to a close, engage in the tradition of drawing Hafez divinations, reflecting on the poetry and the promise of the returning light.

  7. Dawn

    Welcoming the Sunrise

    Witness the first light of dawn, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and the renewal of hope, marking the end of your Yalda Night celebration.

May your Yalda Night be filled with warmth, joy, and the promise of brighter days ahead.
